submitted.rationale: Index 22 (Pb 0.339) had the highest measured EQE, 0.0585%. It lies at the PbSb2O6 stoichiometry. MACE puts PbSb2O6 on the convex hull, and MEGNet gives it an HSE gap of 2.69 eV, so it absorbs the 3.2 eV light. EQE was lower on both sides: 0.022% at Pb 0.50 and 0.032% at Pb 0.29. That suggests a peak near PbSb2O6.

rejected.reason: Pb2Sb2O7 pyrochlore composition; measured EQE 0.022%, lower than index 22
Sb-rich beyond PbSb2O6; measured EQE 0.032%, probably diluted by a wide-gap Sb oxide phase
Pb-rich end, not measured; PbO's predicted gap (3.36 eV) is above the 3.2 eV photon energy, so it should absorb poorly

consultations.verdict: Support: Pb2Sb2O7 (Pb 0.5) is on hull per MACE with HSE gap ~2.5 eV, absorbing at 3.2 eV; index 14 (Pb 0.498) sits at its stoichiometry, so single-phase pyrochlore expected.

Support: PbSb2O6 (Pb 0.333) is on hull (MACE) with HSE gap 2.69 eV, which absorbs at 3.2 eV. PbO on the Pb-rich side has a predicted gap of 3.36 eV, above the photon energy, so it is a weak absorber there. That points to the Sb-rich side, and index 22 (Pb 0.339) is closest to PbSb2O6.

Mixed, weakly supportive. Sb2O3 (3.77 eV) would not absorb at 3.2 eV, but mixed-valence Sb oxide (1.77 eV) would. Past PbSb2O6, a small amount of an Sb-oxide second phase could add absorption or form a heterojunction. EQE rose 2.7x from Pb 0.50 to Pb 0.34, so the Sb-rich end at Pb ~0.29 is the best remaining bet.
